intro_fa: ملا نصرالدین ده خر دارد، اما هر بار که حساب می‌کند، نُه خر است! یک قصه خنده‌دار کهنه.
say_en: Mulla Nasruddin Counts His Donkeys
show_en: Mulla Nasruddin Counts His Donkeys

say_en: Mulla Nasruddin lives in a small village. One day he goes to the town. He buys ten donkeys at the market. Ten good, grey donkeys! "Now I am a rich man," he says. He sits on one donkey and starts to go home.
show_en: Mulla Nasruddin lives in a small village. One day he goes to the town. He buys ten donkeys at the market. Ten good, grey donkeys! "Now I am a rich man," he says. He sits on one donkey and starts to go home.

say_en: On the road Nasruddin thinks: "Are all my donkeys here?" He looks at the donkeys in front of him and counts. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. Nine? Only nine! Where is donkey number ten?"
show_en: On the road Nasruddin thinks: "Are all my donkeys here?" He looks at the donkeys in front of him and counts. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine. Nine? Only nine! Where is donkey number ten?"

say_en: He can see nine donkeys.
show_en: He can see nine donkeys.

say_en: Nasruddin gets down from his donkey. He looks behind the trees. He looks behind the stones. No donkey. He comes back and counts again. "One, two, three... eight, nine, ten. Ten! They are all here. Good!"
show_en: Nasruddin gets down from his donkey. He looks behind the trees. He looks behind the stones. No donkey. He comes back and counts again. "One, two, three... eight, nine, ten. Ten! They are all here. Good!"

say_en: How many donkeys does Nasruddin buy?
show_en: How many donkeys does Nasruddin buy?

say_en: He sits on his donkey again, and they walk on. After an hour he thinks: "Let me count again." He counts: "One, two, three... seven, eight, nine. Nine again! One donkey is lost!" He gets down. He counts. Ten!
show_en: He sits on his donkey again, and they walk on. After an hour he thinks: "Let me count again." He counts: "One, two, three... seven, eight, nine. Nine again! One donkey is lost!" He gets down. He counts. Ten!

say_en: "What is this?" says Nasruddin. "When I sit on my donkey, I have nine donkeys. When I walk, I have ten. Up, nine. Down, ten!" He thinks for a long time. "I know," he says. "I must walk. It is better to walk and have ten donkeys."
show_en: "What is this?" says Nasruddin. "When I sit on my donkey, I have nine donkeys. When I walk, I have ten. Up, nine. Down, ten!" He thinks for a long time. "I know," he says. "I must walk. It is better to walk and have ten donkeys."

say_en: So Nasruddin walks. The road is long and the sun is hot. He is tired and his feet hurt. In the evening he comes to his village. His wife is at the door. "Why do you walk?" she asks. "You have ten donkeys!"
show_en: So Nasruddin walks. The road is long and the sun is hot. He is tired and his feet hurt. In the evening he comes to his village. His wife is at the door. "Why do you walk?" she asks. "You have ten donkeys!"

say_en: "Ten when I walk," says Nasruddin. "Nine when I sit." His wife looks at him. Then she laughs and laughs. "You don't count the donkey under you!" Nasruddin looks at the donkey. He looks at his feet. "Oh," he says.
show_en: "Ten when I walk," says Nasruddin. "Nine when I sit." His wife looks at him. Then she laughs and laughs. "You don't count the donkey under you!" Nasruddin looks at the donkey. He looks at his feet. "Oh," he says.

say_en: Where is donkey number ten?
show_en: Where is donkey number ten?

intro_fa: ملا نصرالدین با کالای کهنه به مهمانی می‌رود و هیچ کس او را نمی‌بیند. با بالاپوش نو چه می‌شود؟ یک قصه کهنه.
say_en: Nasruddin's Coat
show_en: Nasruddin's Coat

say_en: A rich man in the village has a big dinner on Thursday evening. Everyone can come. Mulla Nasruddin works in his field all day. At six o'clock he looks at the sun. "Oh! The dinner!" He has no time to wash or to change his clothes.
show_en: A rich man in the village has a big dinner on Thursday evening. Everyone can come. Mulla Nasruddin works in his field all day. At six o'clock he looks at the sun. "Oh! The dinner!" He has no time to wash or to change his clothes.

say_en: Nasruddin runs to the rich man's house in his old work clothes. His shirt is brown with dust. His shoes are dirty. His old coat has three holes. "Good evening!" he says. But nobody looks at him. Nobody says hello.
show_en: Nasruddin runs to the rich man's house in his old work clothes. His shirt is brown with dust. His shoes are dirty. His old coat has three holes. "Good evening!" he says. But nobody looks at him. Nobody says hello.

say_en: The other men sit near the food. They eat rice and meat. Nasruddin sits by the door. Nobody gives him a plate. Nobody gives him tea. He waits and waits. He is very hungry. Then he stands up and goes home.
show_en: The other men sit near the food. They eat rice and meat. Nasruddin sits by the door. Nobody gives him a plate. Nobody gives him tea. He waits and waits. He is very hungry. Then he stands up and goes home.

say_en: Why does nobody look at Nasruddin?
say_fa: چرا هیچ کس به ملا نصرالدین نگاه نمی‌کند؟
show_en: Why does nobody look at Nasruddin?
choices: t:he is late|t:he is small|t:old clothes
wrong_say_fa: نه. کالای او کهنه و چتل است، پس مردم به او نگاه نمی‌کنند. دوباره بخوان و جواب درست را انتخاب کن.

say_en: At home Nasruddin washes his face and his hands. He combs his hair. He puts on a clean white shirt and good shoes. Then he opens a big box and takes out his best coat. It is brown and warm, with three big buttons.
show_en: At home Nasruddin washes his face and his hands. He combs his hair. He puts on a clean white shirt and good shoes. Then he opens a big box and takes out his best coat. It is brown and warm, with three big buttons.

say_en: This is his best coat.
show_en: This is his best coat.

say_en: Nasruddin goes back to the dinner. Now everyone looks at him. "Good evening, Mulla! Come in, come in!" The rich man gives him the best place. They give him rice, meat, bread and sweet tea. "Eat, Mulla, please eat!"
show_en: Nasruddin goes back to the dinner. Now everyone looks at him. "Good evening, Mulla! Come in, come in!" The rich man gives him the best place. They give him rice, meat, bread and sweet tea. "Eat, Mulla, please eat!"

say_en: Nasruddin takes some rice. But he does not eat it. He puts it on his coat! He puts meat in the pocket. He puts the arm of the coat into the soup. "Eat, my coat, eat!" he says. "Eat, my good coat!"
show_en: Nasruddin takes some rice. But he does not eat it. He puts it on his coat! He puts meat in the pocket. He puts the arm of the coat into the soup. "Eat, my coat, eat!" he says. "Eat, my good coat!"

say_en: Who gets the food from Nasruddin?
say_fa: ملا نصرالدین نان را به کی می‌دهد؟
show_en: Who gets the food from Nasruddin?
wrong_say_fa: نه. ملا نصرالدین نان را به بالاپوش خود می‌دهد. دوباره بخوان و جواب درست را انتخاب کن.

say_en: Everyone stops. The room is quiet. "Mulla, what are you doing?" asks the rich man. "Why do you give food to your coat?" Nasruddin looks at him. Then he looks at all the men, one by one.
show_en: Everyone stops. The room is quiet. "Mulla, what are you doing?" asks the rich man. "Why do you give food to your coat?" Nasruddin looks at him. Then he looks at all the men, one by one.

say_en: "In my old coat there is no food for me," he says. "In my good coat there is rice and meat and tea. But I am the same man! So this dinner is for my coat, not for me." The rich man's face is red. "I am sorry, Mulla," he says.
show_en: "In my old coat there is no food for me," he says. "In my good coat there is rice and meat and tea. But I am the same man! So this dinner is for my coat, not for me." The rich man's face is red. "I am sorry, Mulla," he says.

say_en: Why is the rich man's face red?

intro_fa: در یک خانه تاریک یک حیوان بسیار کلان است. چهار طفل به آن دست می‌زنند و هر کدام چیز دیگری می‌گوید. این قصه بسیار کهنه است.
say_en: The Elephant in the Dark
show_en: The Elephant in the Dark

say_en: One evening some men come to the village with a very big animal. It comes from a country far away. Nobody in the village knows this animal. The men put it in an old house for the night. The house has no window. It is very dark.
show_en: One evening some men come to the village with a very big animal. It comes from a country far away. Nobody in the village knows this animal. The men put it in an old house for the night. The house has no window. It is very dark.

say_en: Four children want to see the animal: Soraya, Bashir, Nadia and Yusuf. They go to the old house at night. They open the door. They can't see anything. "Let's touch it," says Soraya. "Then we can know."
show_en: Four children want to see the animal: Soraya, Bashir, Nadia and Yusuf. They go to the old house at night. They open the door. They can't see anything. "Let's touch it," says Soraya. "Then we can know."

say_en: Soraya puts out her hand. She touches the animal's nose. It is long and it moves. "Oh!" she says. "This animal is like a big snake!" Bashir touches an ear. It is big and thin. "No," he says. "It is like a big leaf."
show_en: Soraya puts out her hand. She touches the animal's nose. It is long and it moves. "Oh!" she says. "This animal is like a big snake!" Bashir touches an ear. It is big and thin. "No," he says. "It is like a big leaf."

show_en: "A snake!" "A leaf!" "A tree!" "A wall!" Four children, four different animals! The friends are not happy with each other. Everyone says: "I am right! My hand knows!" They talk and talk. Nobody listens.

say_en: Then Soraya's grandmother comes with a candle. "Why all this noise?" she asks. She lifts the candle. Now the room is not dark. The children see a long nose, two big ears, four tall legs and a big grey body. It is an elephant!
show_en: Then Soraya's grandmother comes with a candle. "Why all this noise?" she asks. She lifts the candle. Now the room is not dark. The children see a long nose, two big ears, four tall legs and a big grey body. It is an elephant!

intro_fa: یک زن مسافر گرسنه است و فقط یک سنگ دارد. آیا از سنگ شوربا جور می‌شود؟ این قصه کهنه از اروپا آمده است.
say_en: Stone Soup
show_en: Stone Soup

say_en: It is a cold evening. An old woman walks into a small village in the mountains. She comes from far away. She is tired and very hungry. She has a bag on her back. In the bag there is a pot, a spoon and one grey stone.
show_en: It is a cold evening. An old woman walks into a small village in the mountains. She comes from far away. She is tired and very hungry. She has a bag on her back. In the bag there is a pot, a spoon and one grey stone.

say_en: She goes from door to door. "Good evening. Do you have a little food for me?" "Sorry, no," says the man in the first house. "No food here," says the woman in the second house. It is a hard winter. Everyone keeps the food for the family.
show_en: She goes from door to door. "Good evening. Do you have a little food for me?" "Sorry, no," says the man in the first house. "No food here," says the woman in the second house. It is a hard winter. Everyone keeps the food for the family.

say_en: The old woman is not sad. She goes to the middle of the village. She makes a small fire. She puts water in her pot and puts the pot on the fire. Then she takes the stone from her bag and drops it into the pot.
show_en: The old woman is not sad. She goes to the middle of the village. She makes a small fire. She puts water in her pot and puts the pot on the fire. Then she takes the stone from her bag and drops it into the pot.

show_en: A girl comes out of a house. Her name is Farida. "What are you cooking?" she asks. "Stone soup," says the old woman. "It is very good. But with a carrot it is better." "We have a carrot!" says Farida. She runs home and brings it.

say_en: Now more people come and look. "Stone soup? What is that?" "It is good," says the old woman. "But with an onion it is better." A man brings two onions. A boy brings three potatoes. A grandmother brings a tomato and some salt.
show_en: Now more people come and look. "Stone soup? What is that?" "It is good," says the old woman. "But with an onion it is better." A man brings two onions. A boy brings three potatoes. A grandmother brings a tomato and some salt.

show_en: The soup cooks on the fire. It smells very good. Somebody brings bread. Somebody brings plates and spoons. Somebody brings a carpet. Now all the village sits by the fire. The old woman gives soup to everyone, and they eat together.

say_en: "This is the best soup of the winter!" say the people. "And it comes from a stone!" The old woman laughs. She takes the stone out of the pot. She washes it and puts it back in her bag.
show_en: "This is the best soup of the winter!" say the people. "And it comes from a stone!" The old woman laughs. She takes the stone out of the pot. She washes it and puts it back in her bag.

say_en: Farida looks at the stone. She looks at the people by the fire. "It is not the stone," she says slowly. "It is us. Everyone gives a little, and then there is food for all." The old woman smiles. "Clever girl," she says.

say_en: Seven Days, Seven Eggs
show_en: Seven Days, Seven Eggs

say_en: Shirin is twelve. She likes school and she likes to write. But her notebook is full. Every page has words on it. In the village shop there is a new notebook, a blue one. "How much is it?" asks Shirin. "Seven eggs," says the shopkeeper.
show_en: Shirin is twelve. She likes school and she likes to write. But her notebook is full. Every page has words on it. In the village shop there is a new notebook, a blue one. "How much is it?" asks Shirin. "Seven eggs," says the shopkeeper.

say_en: Shirin has no money and no eggs. But she has a small brown hen. Every morning it gives one egg, and Shirin eats it for breakfast. "Mother, can I keep my eggs this week?" "Yes," says Mother. "But then you have only bread for breakfast."
show_en: Shirin has no money and no eggs. But she has a small brown hen. Every morning it gives one egg, and Shirin eats it for breakfast. "Mother, can I keep my eggs this week?" "Yes," says Mother. "But then you have only bread for breakfast."

show_en: How many eggs does the shopkeeper want?

say_en: On Saturday the hen gives an egg. Shirin puts it in a basket. On Sunday, one more. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday: three, four, five eggs. Every morning Shirin eats only bread. Every morning she counts her eggs. On Thursday there are six.
show_en: On Saturday the hen gives an egg. Shirin puts it in a basket. On Sunday, one more. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday: three, four, five eggs. Every morning Shirin eats only bread. Every morning she counts her eggs. On Thursday there are six.

say_en: Shirin sits down by the door with her basket. Six eggs. Not seven. Her eyes are wet. Her small brother Omid comes out of the house. "Why are you sad?" he asks. "The hen is tired today," says Shirin. "And I can't buy my notebook."
